text: Which is the strongest argument against using reflection in ordinary application code?
choices: It is forty to sixty times slower than a direct call, which no program can afford.
The module system will eventually forbid it, so such code has no future.
It requires catching three checked exceptions, which makes the code verbose.
Every compile-time check is suspended — a misspelled method name becomes a run-time exception, and renaming in an IDE misses it.
explanation: The speed cost is real but usually irrelevant; the safety cost is not. Rename a method and every ordinary call site updates while the string in a reflective call does not. It also breaks find-usages, dead-code elimination, obfuscation, and ahead-of-time compilation — which is why the ecosystem has spent years moving reflective work to compile-time code generation. The rule: if you know the class at compile time, call the method.
